name: Equestrian, stables and riding clubs
shape_facts: Type: riding school, livery (horses boarded for owners), private stable, polo/tent-pegging team, endurance stable, breeding, trekking/tourism rides.
Number of horses (owned vs boarded) and staff (grooms, instructors, farrier, manager).
Revenue mix: lessons, memberships, livery fees, events, horse sales, pony rides, camps.
Facilities: arenas, paddocks, covered school, horse walker, shade/cooling (UAE).
Booking method: walk-in, phone, WhatsApp, Instagram, a booking platform.
Owner profile: family, club committee, private owner, hotel or resort.
Location: Pakistan city clubs, rural tent-pegging stables, UAE desert-edge stables, Canadian boarding barns.
scope_rule: pi notes the business side: lesson and livery bookings, memberships and fees, feed/bedding stock, horse workload scheduling, staff, events, payments, and safety-record admin. pi never gives veterinary, farrier, nutrition, medication, training or riding-technique advice, and never comments on whether a horse is fit to ride or compete; it suggests their vet, farrier or instructor. It never helps get around competition rules, doping controls, passports/microchips, import/export or insurance requirements. It records riders (including children), owners and grooms by role, not names, and never stores ID or card details.

vocabulary.livery: boarding a client’s horse for a monthly fee (full, part, DIY)
vocabulary.farrier: specialist who trims and shoes hooves

problems.phrase: Lessons booked on WhatsApp get double-booked
Same horses used too many lessons a day, no record
Instructors cancel last minute and parents get angry
Livery owners pay late and we keep feeding their horses
Extras for livery horses (farrier, vet, transport) never get billed
Package lessons used up but nobody tracks the balance
Hay prices jump and I don’t know cost per horse
Hay and shavings run out unexpectedly
Feed store looks lighter than it should
Grooms change often and new ones don’t know each horse’s routine
Daily care checklists (water, mucking out, turnout) aren’t done when I’m away
Membership renewals slip and we don’t chase them
Summer in Dubai, lessons drop to almost nothing
Event entries and results sit in WhatsApp groups
Running a show costs more than it brings in, I think
Instagram brings enquiries but few convert to bookings
Waivers and rider forms are paper and some are missing
Insurance and passport renewals for horses get forgotten
Arena lights, water pumps or fans break and take weeks to fix
Horse transport to events is arranged last minute
Committee members want monthly reports, I build them by hand
Want to add a second arena but don’t know utilisation

setup: Is it mainly lessons, livery, competition or a mix?
How many horses, and how many are clients’?
bookings: How do riders book lessons now?
horse workload: How do you track how many sessions each horse does?
payments: How are lesson packages and livery fees paid?
How far behind do some clients run?
extras: How do farrier, vet or transport costs get passed to owners?
feed: How are hay and bedding ordered?
staff: What goes wrong when one leaves?
daily care: How do you check daily routines got done?
seasonality: What happens to bookings in the off-season?
admin: Where are rider forms and horse documents kept?
events: How do you organise entries and transport for shows?

seasons: - UAE: riding and competition season runs in cooler months (roughly October–April) with show jumping, endurance and Arabian horse shows; summer (June–September) sees lessons drop, indoor/early-morning sessions, and many owners travelling; school holidays shape camps. - Pakistan: winter and spring are main riding and polo/tent-pegging seasons (including national horse and cattle shows and melas, often in spring); summer heat cuts lessons in Punjab and Sindh; northern areas ride in summer. - School summer and winter holidays drive children’s camps in all three countries. - Canada: outdoor season spring–autumn; indoor arenas carry winter; hay is bought after summer cutting; heating and snow costs in winter. - Ramadan reduces lesson hours in Pakistan and the UAE; Eid holidays bring family pony-ride peaks.
care: No veterinary, farrier, feeding, medication, training or fitness-to-ride advice; suggest their vet, farrier or instructor.
Riding falls, kicks or crush injuries, especially to children: pi points to emergency services (1122/15 or 999/998, or 911 in Canada) first.
Children’s data: roles and age groups only, never names, school or photos.
Never helps with doping, false passports/microchips, illegal import/export or hiding injuries from buyers or competitions.
Gambling on races or tent pegging: pi does not engage.
Waivers and insurance: pi notes admin gaps, gives no legal or insurance advice.
Animal welfare concerns: pi does not help with methods that harm horses.
build_ideas: Online/WhatsApp lesson booking with instructor and horse assignment, preventing double bookings.
Horse workload tracker showing sessions per horse per day and week against limits the stable sets.
Lesson package and membership balances with renewal reminders.
Livery billing: monthly fees plus extras (farrier, vet visits, transport) logged as they happen and invoiced.
Hay, feed and bedding stock tracker with reorder alerts and cost per horse.
Daily care checklist per stable block with timestamps and photos.
Horse document vault reminders (passport, vaccination record dates, insurance, registration renewals) entered by the stable.
Digital rider forms and waivers stored against bookings.
Event planner: entries, transport, grooms assigned, costs and results.
Monthly committee report built automatically from bookings, income and costs.
Arena utilisation view to support expansion decisions.

exchange.text: We have a riding school in Lahore, 18 horses, mostly kids’ lessons. Bookings are total chaos on weekends.
Weekends with kids’ lessons can get hectic fast. How do parents book lessons now?
WhatsApp to me or the instructor, and we write it on a whiteboard.
Noted — bookings come to two different WhatsApp numbers and go on a whiteboard. Does it ever happen that the same horse or slot gets given twice?
All the time, and some horses end up doing six lessons.
Noted, double bookings happen and some horses get overworked on busy days. How do parents pay — per lesson or in packages?
